parsed.answer: This looks like a known problem: Windows Terminal crashing with an access violation (0xc0000005) in Microsoft.Terminal.Control.dll when a tab is dragged or merged into another window (terminal#17246, terminal#19383). In terminal#17246 the cause was traced to a null pointer dereference: when a tab is torn off or closed, XAML calls OnCreateAutomationPeer on a TermControl that has no interactivity attached, and a fix was proposed in #17251. That ticket was reported as fatal only for some drag cases and notes that other crash scenarios remained, so it is not a complete fix. terminal#19383 reports a similar crash during a merge on 1.22, with a different fault in the renderer (AtlasEngine::PaintCursor). It has no resolution in the ticket text shown to me. Neither ticket gives a workaround or a confirmed fix for 1.24. Please comment on terminal#19383 (or terminal#17246) with your build, the fault offset 0x2c924, and the faulting stack from your dump. You can run !analyze -v in WinDbg on the dump and share only the stack and failure bucket, which avoids exposing scrollback. Until a fix is available, avoid drag-merging tabs between windows, especially after long sessions with large scrollback. Instead, open a new tab in the target window. Because all windows share one process, a crash takes them all down, so save any important work first.
